newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide advertising rises eight percent in 1995.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide advertising rises eight percent in 1995.

text.p: Worldwide advertising expenditure rose eight percent from 1994 to 1995, with Estonia claiming the world's fastest-growing advertising market that year, according to a new report released on Tuesday.
World Advertising Trends, released by NTC Publications Ltd, said above-the-line advertising for 79 countries rose to about $250 billion in 1995.
Estonia had the highest rise in advertising expenditure, rising 150 percent in 1995, while Uganda and Zambia each posted growth of more than 50 percent in real terms, the report added.

NTC, which has been publishing the annual World Advertising Trends since 1987, said advertising expenditure in China rose 880 percent between 1987 and 1995. Argentina had the second-highest growth in the period, rising 600 percent.

Switzerland had the highest per capita advertising spending at $415 per head. The U.S., Japan and Hong Kong each had per capita advertising spending of more than $300. Advertising spending of more than $100 per head was recorded in 26 countries, while seven countries had per capita expenditure of less than $1. The Ivory Coast was the poorest country with only five cents per capita.

Print advertising commanded just over half the total market in 1995, accounting for 50.7 percent and expenditure of $125 billion. Television was the second largest advertising market, claiming $89 billion, but was the fastest-growing medium, rising to a 36.4 percent market share in 1995 from 30 percent in 1987.
